focus: Triggers and path filters; the Trigger Index Rebuild burst
answeredQuestions: Which triggers and path filters cause needless runs, including the run burst after each Trigger Index Rebuild commit?

graphEvents.label: Which triggers and path filters cause needless runs, including the rebuild burst
Rebuild fan-out is 51.4% of billed minutes
spec-kit-check is triggered by the generated index
Nine workflows have no push path filter

label: 45.2% of the commits in the measured 23.5 h window (33 of 73 distinct headSha) are machine-generated trigger-index rebuild commits, and every one of them starts exactly 14 workflows.
The rebuild fan-out costs ~1955 billed runner-minutes/day, 51.4% of the 3812 min/day total: 58.0 billed min per rebuild commit against 45.3 for an ordinary commit.

spec-kit-check fires on every rebuild commit because the generated trigger index lives at .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/data/trigger-index.json, which its own push path filter matches; that one workflow is 25.0 of the 58.0 min per rebuild commit, ~825 min/day.

Nine of the 33 workflows have no push path filter at all (sk-doc-script-tests, command-tree-parity, dispatch-enforcement-guard, gate-inputs, rule-canary-sync, message-contract, changed-packet-validation, advisory-checks, playbook-operator-contract), so they re-run on every rebuild commit for 25.0 of its 58.0 min; eight other workflows with real path filters recorded zero runs across all 33 rebuild commits, proving the mechanism works in-repo.
32 of the 33 workflows declare no concurrency group; only trigger-index-rebuild has one (cancel-in-progress: false). Superseded pushes therefore run to completion and bill in full.

The README's GITHUB_TOKEN sentence describes only the fallback path: the push step authenticates with secrets.TRIGGER_INDEX_PUSH_TOKEN, and the 33 x 14 started runs confirm those pushes do trigger workflows, so the trailer loop guard at trigger-index-rebuild.yml:33 is load-bearing and its 33 skipped runs are not free (they still consume a run slot).
message-contract triggers on branches ['**'], every branch in the repository, not just main and skilled/**; it is 2.0 min per commit and 73 of 73 commits fire it.

direction: That a path filter already excludes index-only rebuild commits from the push gates (iteration 001 F7 hypothesis)
reason: Disproved by measurement: 33 of 73 distinct headSha are rebuild commits and every one starts exactly 14 workflows with zero variance; spec-kit-check's filter matches the generated index path itself.

direction: Suppressing the burst by adding paths-ignore to all 13 affected push triggers instead of skipping the rebuild commit
reason: Same saving (1955 min/day) at 13 file edits and a per-file parity argument, versus one commit-message token in the workflow that already owns the generated commit; the paths-ignore route also has to special-case playbook-operator-contract, whose unfiltered trigger is documented as intentional.
